case_title: Chandra Bhawan Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (Tribhuwan Singh was the victim's husband); Relative (Chandra Bhawan Singh was brother-in-law and Makoi Devi mother-in-law); prior dowry harassment by in-laws
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.201; Dowry Prohibition Act s.4 (charged)
evidence_type: Circumstantial (principal basis); medical (post-mortem, gunshot injuries); recovery (gun); ballistic report; oral testimony of the victim's brother (PW-1) on dowry demand
aggravating_circumstances: Seven gunshot injuries on the victim; death inside the in-laws' house; sustained dowry demands and harassment
trial_court_outcome: Jwala Singh acquitted; Tribhuwan Singh convicted under IPC s.302/34, life imprisonment and Rs 5000 fine; Chandra Bhawan Singh convicted under IPC s.302/34 (life) and s.201 (five years RI), concurrent; Makoi Devi convicted under s.302/34 (life)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed for Tribhuwan Singh and Chandra Bhawan Singh, conviction and sentence confirmed; appeal allowed and Makoi Devi acquitted
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (both appellants); IPC s.201 (Chandra Bhawan Singh)
neutral_facts: The victim was married and lived in the household of her in-laws, which included her husband, mother-in-law and brother-in-law. Family members of the victim alleged that the in-laws harassed her for failing to bring a motorcycle as dowry. Because of the harassment she returned to her parents' house. About three days later, two of the accused brought her back to the in-laws' house. On 18.03.1984 the victim was found dead inside that house, having suffered gunshot injuries, and her body lay in the courtyard. A first information report was lodged the same day by one of the accused, stating that the victim had committed suicide by gunshot. A separate report was registered on the basis of a complaint by the village headman. The victim's brother also lodged a report that day alleging that all four accused had killed her because their dowry demand was not met. The accused were arrested on 19/20.04.1984. A gun was recovered from the house on the instance of one accused. The post-mortem examination found that the victim had been murdered. Ballistic experts examined the weapon, and statements were recorded from the accused and other witnesses. The police filed the charge sheet on 09.06.1984.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by gunshot; seven gunshot injuries on the body
number_of_offences: 3 charged (IPC s.302/34, IPC s.201, DP Act s.4); 2 convictions finally upheld for Chandra Bhawan Singh (IPC s.302/34 and s.201); 1 finally upheld for Tribhuwan Singh (IPC s.302/34)
motive: Dowry demand (motorcycle) and harassment of the victim by the in-laws, accepted by the Court
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-1 (victim's brother) on dowry demand and harassment; medical evidence of multiple gunshot injuries; DBBL gun use; the seven circumstances relied on by the High Court; the appellants' failure to explain under s.313 CrPC; Tribhuwan Singh's unproved alibi
witness_credibility: PW-1 (victim's brother, complainant) found natural, consistent and without material contradiction; his evidence accepted. Defence suicide story found wholly unbelievable on the record
post_offence_conduct: Chandra Bhawan Singh lodged the first FIR claiming suicide, which the Court found false and intended to divert police attention; both accused gave no explanation under s.313 CrPC; Tribhuwan Singh's alibi was not proved
trial_duration: offence: 18.03.1984 (date victim found dead; date of death not separately stated); trial judgment: 07.05.1986; High Court: 20.05.2014; Supreme Court: May 01, 2018
legal_representation: For accused: Nagendra Rai, Sr. Adv. (with others). For State: Ratnakar Dash, Sr. Adv. (with others)
investigation_status: FIR lodged 18.03.1984 (PS Kishanpur); accused arrested 19/20.04.1984; ballistic report obtained; challan filed 09.06.1984; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (Additional Sessions Judge, Fatehpur, 07.05.1986): convicted; High Court (20.05.2014): appeal dismissed, conviction confirmed; Supreme Court: appeals dismissed, convictions upheld
prosecution_argument: Concurrent findings of both courts below were correct and should not be interfered with; the appeals should be dismissed
defence_argument: Conviction, though concurrent, is not factually or legally sustainable; chain of circumstances not proved; the victim committed suicide
legal_principle_applied: Article 136: slow to interfere with concurrent findings; no de novo appreciation unless perversity or absurdity or relevant evidence ignored. Circumstantial evidence test: chain of events directly connected with the incident, proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt; s.313 CrPC failure to explain may complete the chain
